key_insight: PhysForge separates functional design from physics specification to generate 3D assets that are both geometrically plausible and behaviorally accurate for interaction. A decoupled two-stage pipeline plus a large PhysDB enables scalable creation of physics-grounded assets.
problem_solved: Existing 3D asset generation focuses on static geometry and ignores functional and hierarchical physical properties, preventing realistic interactions in virtual worlds and embodied AI.
method: Decoupled two-stage framework: (1) generate functionally plausible geometry guided by functional logic, (2) assign hierarchical physics properties (materials, mass, constraints) for interaction.
Train and validate using PhysDB — a large dataset of ~150,000 assets annotated with a four-tier physics/functional hierarchy to teach asset-function-physics mappings.
Optimize for interactive behavior by evaluating simulated affordances and dynamics, closing the loop between geometry and physics specification.
impact: Enables scalable creation of interactive, physically consistent 3D assets for simulators and embodied agents, reducing manual authoring and improving realism for downstream tasks like robotics, games, and virtual training.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing Stage 1 (functional geometry) -> Stage 2 (hierarchical physics) -> interactive simulation

Before/after comparison of static geometry vs physics-grounded behavior (e.g., object interacting in simulator)
Hierarchy tree/iconography illustrating multi-level physical properties (material, mass, constraints, affordances)
paper_title: PhysForge: Generating Physics-Grounded 3D Assets for Interactive Virtual World
paper_authors: Yunhan Yang, Chunshi Wang, Junliang Ye, Yang Li, Zanxin Chen
